name: item_acen_pivot
description: Frozen reference behaviour: with the selection type Item, the action centre is the item's world PIVOT — position + pivot — and NOT the geometry's world bounding-box centre, not the position alone, and not the world origin. The rig is built so all four candidates are DIFFERENT numbers; an earlier rig had pos = pivot = (0,0,0) and could not tell them apart.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted; no viewport drag). The rig was deliberately rebuilt so the four candidate laws predict four distinct points.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (scripts + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: Seven consecutive evaluated frames, all identical, under two different transform configurations. A sensitivity control was run in the same session: forcing the action centre to an explicit world-origin mode moved the measured point to (0,0,0), so the channel is live and the agreement is not an insensitive read. A second control candidate was attempted first and turned out to name a command that does not exist — a DEAD control, not an insensitive channel; it was re-run with a valid one.

rig.comment: One item. Its mesh is a unit cube whose LOCAL centre is (3,0,0) — displaced on purpose so the geometry-derived candidate cannot coincide with the pivot-derived one.

control.comment: Sensitivity control from the same capture: with the action-centre mode forced to an explicit world-origin mode, the measured point MOVES. Without this the seven identical frames would not distinguish 'the law is pos+pivot' from 'this channel never changes'.

vibe3d_sensitivity.comment: Not a reference measurement -- a vibe3d-side vacuity guard. On this SAME rig and the SAME read, switching the subject from items to mesh components makes the rejected geometry-derived candidate actually appear, proving that branch is reachable and that the item answer is a real election rather than the only value this endpoint can produce. The value is the mesh's local bbox centre (3,0,0) carried through the item matrix, i.e. `rejected[geometry world bounding-box centre]` above, EXACTLY -- which makes this guard stronger than it was: the component branch now lands on a candidate the reference itself named and rejected.
vibe3d_sensitivity.updated: Task 0649. This field read (3,0,0) -- the mesh's own undisplaced coordinates -- on the premise, stated in the previous comment, that 'the item transform is render-only, so the component branch reads the mesh's own coordinates'. That premise is what 0649 removed: the geometry-derived action centre is published in WORLD space, so the component branch now reads (3,2,0). The guard's INTENT is unchanged and it still discriminates -- (3,2,0) differs from the item centre (0,2,3).

classification.detail: vibe3d's item-mode action centre reads pos + pivot and produces (0,2,3) on this rig — identical to the reference. This fixture is a LIVE test that must pass.
